production_audit.ownership_and_callgraph: PyRequest.generate/count/explain and PyDiagramSet.build/PyBuiltDiagramSet.select/group all enter execution::execute. It creates ProgressDelivery once at execution.rs:206. Native service_caller invokes the same instance at :340 and the post-join final flush at :471. WASM uses an Arc clone at :221/:239; source inspected only for WASM. Only the unit test constructs a separate delivery object for its independent execution.
production_audit.state_lifetime: The persistent AtomicBool belongs to the per-execution owner, starts false for each separate execute, and survives every pending.take. Relaxed is adequate because caller-thread deliveries are serialized. Run cancellation keeps its existing token synchronization. No second queue, alternate production dispatcher, public compatibility API, or per-batch reconstruction.
production_audit.gil_and_locks: PendingProgress lock is released before Python callbacks. Native work remains under py.detach and Python progress is attached on the invoking OS thread. Workers only record snapshots and request synchronized replies. Existing callback/predicate routing is unchanged; module-scope imports and a private inherent method follow owner/import policy.
production_audit.cancellation_and_done: Only an actual Python False sets callback suppression and cancels the token. Explicit token cancellation with None remains distinct. Nonterminals are skipped across drains; Done still passes. Native Done synchronization receives Cancel and report.completed is finalized false after cancellation; retained_count and Done count refer to returned diagrams.
production_audit.exceptions_and_cleanup: Callback errors/invalid returns stop delivery and preserve original errors; a Done exception after False retains precedence. The existing scoped generation worker and optional predicate worker are joined before return, cancellation/error replies continue to unblock work, and final drain is skipped when interruption is present. Spinner error cleanup is unchanged. Fresh controls cover signal handling, callback error identity, worker permission, GC/view expiry and terminal exceptions.

controlled_red_qualification.schedule: Worker records Skeletons and blocks on continue_receiver. First ready handshake precedes deliver(false). Caller waits for that delivery to return and asserts cancelled, then sends continue. Worker records Dressing/Prepare/Done and signals ready. Only then caller forces the second drain, joins worker, and checks a third empty drain. No sleeps or wall-clock assertions determine this ordering.
controlled_red_qualification.mutation: The red production method replaces execution-persistent callback_cancelled with local terminal_only=false inside each delivery. The controlled Rust test has the same callback, channels, snapshots and assertion; its only necessary source difference is initialization of the restored member in green. Red-to-green also has a receipt and a redundant globals()[fk] assignment in the separate real-generation Python fixture, which this controlled Rust test does not load. These do not cause the controlled failure.
